clue.text: Attendant put on petticoat or an unwanted shift

indicators.note: the attendant is placed after (put on to) the petticoat in the charade

parts.note: a slip is a petticoat or underskirt
a page is a young attendant or servant

explanation.surface: A servant pulls on an underskirt, or perhaps some unwelcome change of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like another garment beside the petticoat, but here it means a movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippage is a gradual unwanted movement or decline, such as a sliding shift in position or schedule.

clue.text: In the main, they catch personnel interrupting new temps in seconds

indicators.note: the personnel letters break into the middle of the jumbled letters
new means a fresh form, so temps and in are rearranged

parts.note: HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: HR staff barge in on freshly hired temporary workers, all within seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal and 'interrupting' the insertion. 'The main' is an old poetic name for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is an old word for the open sea, where shrimp nets are used to catch small crustaceans.

clue.text: Where Marxists govern, right-winger's brooding has such an effect

parts.note: in Cuba is where a communist, Marxist government rules
a Tory is a right-winger, a British Conservative

explanation.surface: Under communist rule, a conservative's dark mood has a certain impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brooding' looks like moody thinking, but it is sitting on eggs to hatch them.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubatory describes incubation, the warming that hatches eggs, which is the effect a brooding bird has.

clue.text: Nancy's old serving man turned up to frame painting

indicators.note: the turned letters frame, or surround, the painting word
turned means flipped round, so the letters of up are read backwards

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: An old manservant in Nancy turns up to put a picture in a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' signals the reversal and 'to frame' the container. Nancy is a city in France, so 'Nancy's' means French.
explanation.definitionFit: Poilu was the nickname of the French infantryman in World War I, so an old French serviceman.

clue.text: Artist acquires a bit of English capital

parts.note: gains means acquires
London is divided into boroughs, so a borough is a part of the English capital

explanation.surface: A painter buys up a piece of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gainsborough was an eighteenth-century English painter of portraits and landscapes.

clue.text: Reclining, take a pew and mug for aperitif

indicators.note: something reclining lies back, so in this clue the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to take a pew is to sit down
a mug is a dupe or fool, a sap

explanation.surface: Someone lounges in a seat with a mug, ready for a drink before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reclining' signals the reversal: lying back, the whole charade is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastis is an aniseed-flavoured French spirit typically drunk before a meal, so it is an example of an aperitif.

clue.text: Opt against playing, leaving golf course

indicators.note: playing about with the words, so their letters are rearranged
leaving means the golf letter departs from the mix

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone decides not to play, quitting the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opt against playing' looks like declining to play; instead 'playing' rearranges OPT AGAINST and 'leaving' takes out G. 'Golf course' is split.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter of cold meats and vegetables, the first course of a meal.

clue.text: One cuts current outings with enchanting lady

parts.note: trips are outings or excursions
a witch is a woman who casts spells, enchanting people

explanation.surface: Excursions with a charming woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' is electric current, not the present.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip switch is a safety device that automatically breaks an electric circuit when it is overloaded.

clue.text: See 24
Rickety chair upset with jerk

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: A wobbly chair gets knocked over by a sudden jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges CHAIR into RACHI. RACHITIC means affected by rickets, so 'Rickety' is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Rachitic is the medical adjective for having rickets, which is exactly what rickety originally meant.

clue.text: Invader has trouble crossing dry area

indicators.note: the trouble word spans across, so it straddles the dry letters

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol, dry

explanation.surface: An invading force runs into difficulty in a parched region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' signals the container; TT for teetotal is the crossword's usual 'dry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila the Hun led barbarian forces that overran much of the Roman Empire in the fifth century.

clue.text: Not anticipating much, like Robin's correspondence with Doris?

definitions.meaning: living ... means getting by without planning for the future
letters from broadcaster Robin Day to the singer Doris Day would go ...

explanation.walkthrough: Robin Day was a British television interviewer; Doris Day an American singer and actress. The pair never corresponded, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: From day to day is an idiom for living in the present, concerned only with immediate needs.

clue.text: Crowd united in high spirits for band with no B-side?

parts.note: a mob is a crowd

indicators.note: in places the united letter inside the jumbled letters of spirits, after their first letter
high means intoxicated or wild, so the letters of spirits are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to be jumbled
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A crowd cheering a pop group whose single has no flip side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' scrambles SPIRITS into ISSTRIP, with U placed 'in' it. A 'band' is a strip, and a Möbius strip has only one side, so no B-side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Möbius strip is a looped band given a half-twist so it has a single continuous surface, not two sides.

clue.text: Return of cutter riding the waves on the drink

indicators.note: return means going back, so the cutter word is read backwards

parts.note: a saw is a cutting tool
a boat riding the waves is sailing

explanation.surface: A cutter boat sails back out over the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' and 'the drink' both suggest sailing; the cutter is a SAW, and 'the drink' is alcohol, not the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassailing is old-fashioned festive carousing, drinking healths, so being on the drink.

clue.text: Nicely trim dressing nurse cut on new patient

indicators.note: the trim word dresses, or covers, the other letters

parts.note: pert means neat and trim, smartly attractive

indicators.note: on signals the new letter is placed next to the nurse
cut means the nurse word loses its final letter

parts.note: a sister is a senior nurse in British hospitals

explanation.surface: A neat bandage applied by a nurse to a fresh patient's wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like a noun but is the adjective meaning persevering. 'cut' drops the final letter, 'on' joins N, and 'dressing' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Patient in the sense of persevering steadily at long work is close to persistent, as Chambers allows.

clue.text: Excluding top royal commentator

parts.note: not means except or excluding, as in 'everyone not him'
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen, the top royal

explanation.surface: Someone commenting on royal affairs leaves out the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A noter is one who makes notes or remarks, so a commentator or annotator.

clue.text: Stealing hearts, music genre's poetic and lyrical

indicators.note: the genre word steals the hearts letter, taking it inside

parts.note: rap is a music genre, so rap's
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts
odic means relating to odes, so poetic

explanation.surface: A style of music wins people's hearts with its poetic lyrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stealing' puts H inside RAP'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsodic means ecstatically expressive, as in a rhapsody, so effusively lyrical.

clue.text: Following the party line, singles wise to drink last of rum

indicators.note: the singles word takes in, or drinks, the letter from rum

parts.note: ones are singles, single units

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of rum

parts.note: sage means wise

explanation.surface: Unattached people with sense have a final tot of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drink' puts M, picked by 'last of' from rum, inside ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: On message is the political idiom for sticking to the official policy and talking points of one's party.

clue.text: Spanish port I'm leaving without tatty garment on

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the goodbye word goes round the rest

parts.note: ta-ra is a northern British goodbye, said when one is leaving
a rag is a worn, tatty piece of clothing

explanation.surface: Someone departs without putting on a shabby piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so it is the container. Ta-ra is informal northern British for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragona is a city and seaport on the Mediterranean coast of Catalonia, in north-east Spain.

clue.text: Place to drink nothing in current circumstances

parts.note: O, the zero, means nothing
as is means in the present condition, as things stand

explanation.surface: A bar where nothing is served under the present arrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert with water, where travellers and animals drink.

clue.text: Guitarists and a rock star group

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Guitarists and a rock star form a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks like part of 'rock star', but it is the signal to rearrange GUITARISTS + A.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagittarius is a constellation, a group of stars, as well as a sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Sign of decay but not the first

indicators.note: the decay word is used without its opening letter

parts.note: caries is tooth decay

explanation.surface: An indication of rot, though not the earliest one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign of decay' reads as one phrase, but 'Sign' alone is the definition: a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Leader deposed by Jeb Bush oddly loses power

indicators.note: the first letter of Jeb is removed, as a leader is deposed
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of Bush

explanation.surface: A political leader is ousted as Jeb Bush strangely loses influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader deposed by' drops J from JEB; 'oddly' gives BS from BUSH. Jeb Bush is an American politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To ebb is to decline or wane in strength, as a tide flows out.

clue.text: Country bringing down current queen

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing down means moving the current letter lower, to the end

parts.note: Iran is a country
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A nation topples its present queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing down' moves I from the top of IRAN to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is a Hindu queen or the wife of a rajah.

clue.text: Mark bringing flower back? This is sweet

parts.note: a brand is a mark burnt or stamped on

indicators.note: bringing back means the flower is read in reverse

parts.note: a pansy is a garden flower

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a brand mark comes with returning a bloom, which is a nice gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses PANSY to YSNAP, giving BRANDY + SNAP across 24 and 8.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a crisp rolled ginger biscuit, often filled with cream, a classic British sweet treat.

clue.text: Forming a habit to ignore cold food ingredient

indicators.note: to ignore the cold letter is to leave it out

parts.note: something habit-forming is addictive
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A habit-forming snack that disregards a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore' removes C from ADDICTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An additive is a substance put into food to preserve, flavour or colour it, so it is one of the ingredients.

clue.text: See 7
Out loud, I refer to what the Observer must use

indicators.note: out loud means spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: to cite something is to refer to it, so I refer to is I cite

explanation.surface: Speaking aloud, a writer mentions the newspaper's required style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out loud': I CITE sounds like EYESIGHT. The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, but here it is just one who observes.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who observes or watches needs vision, the faculty of seeing with one's eyes.
